messages.content: I can't believe I got promoted — after months of hard work it finally paid off and I'm absolutely ecstatic! I can't wait to dive into the new role, prove my performance was worth it, and start driving even bigger results.

messages.speaker: responder_agent
messages.content:
Huge congratulations — that’s fantastic news! You deserve it after all that hard work.

What’s the new role, and when do you start? If you want, I can help you sketch a 30/60/90-day plan, outline priorities, or draft a short thank-you/intro message for your new team. A few quick ideas to hit the ground running:
- Clarify expectations with your manager and set measurable early goals.
- Meet key stakeholders, learn their priorities, and listen more than you talk at first.
- Identify a few achievable “early wins” to build momentum and credibility.
- Delegate what you can and empower your team; avoid trying to do everything yourself.
- Schedule regular check-ins and carve out time for learning and strategic thinking.

How are you celebrating?

messages.speaker: persona_agent
messages.content: I’m now Senior Product Manager starting next Monday — after months of extra hours and staying late it finally feels like all that effort was worth it and I’m absolutely buzzing! I’d love help sketching a 30/60/90 plan and drafting a short intro/thank-you message so I can hit the ground running.

messages.speaker: responder_agent
messages.content:
Congrats again — that’s awesome. Below is a practical 30/60/90 plan you can take into Monday plus two short message templates (one to your manager/sponsor and one for your new team). If you want, I can customize the plan to your product, team size, and top priorities.

30/60/90-day plan (Senior Product Manager)

Goal structure
- 30 days: Learn, build relationships, and understand the metrics and current roadmap.
- 60 days: Influence direction, secure quick wins, start executing on priorities.
- 90 days: Deliver measurable impact, set longer-term strategy, and establish routines.

First 30 days — Understand & Align
Objectives
- Be fully onboarded on product, customers, metrics, roadmap, and team.
- Build relationships with manager, direct reports, engineers, designers, PM peers, sales/CS, and key execs/stakeholders.

Key activities
- 1:1s: Meet your manager, each direct report, key engineers/designers, product marketing, sales/CS leads, and any major external partners/customers (15–30 min for peers, 45–60 for manager/stakeholders).
- Product deep-dive: Walk through product, code/architecture overview if needed, analytics dashboards, backlog, and current sprint.
- Data & metrics: Review KPIs (activation, retention, engagement, revenue, conversion funnels, cycle time). Understand where product is under/over-performing.
- Customer voices: Read recent support tickets, user interviews, NPS/feedback, and speak to at least 2–3 customers.
- Stakeholder map: Document influence, expectations, and priorities.

Deliverables / success signals
- One-page summary: product state, top 3 risks, top 3 opportunities.
- Relationship map and meeting notes.
- Agreed expectations with manager: success criteria for 30/60/90.

30–60 days — Influence & Deliver early wins
Objectives
- Propose and execute 1–2 high-impact, low-risk improvements.
- Start shaping product priorities and gain support from stakeholders.

Key activities
- Prioritize: Run a lightweight backlog / opportunity review with engineering and design to identify quick wins.
- Small experiments: Launch an experiment or A/B test addressing a major friction (onboarding, pricing page, conversion funnel).
- Roadmap shaping: Draft proposed roadmap adjustments with rationale and metrics.
- Process improvements: Introduce or refine planning cadence, PRD template, or sprint planning if needed.
- Deeper customer validation: Run 3–5 targeted interviews or usability tests for priority features.

Deliverables / success signals
- One executed experiment with baseline and early results.
- Proposed 3–6 month roadmap and resource needs.
- Stakeholder alignment document and updated priorities.

60–90 days — Scale & Cement strategy
Objectives
- Deliver on the priority(s) you committed to, demonstrate measurable impact, and establish long-term planning cadence.

Key activities
- Deliver feature(s) or launch: Oversee rollout, communicate with GTM, monitor KPIs.
- Measure impact: Report results against baseline; iterate on learnings.
- Strategic planning: Present 6–12 month strategy to manager/execs with OKRs and resource ask.
- Team development: Identify hiring/training needs and propose org/process improvements.

Deliverables / success signals
- Measurable impact (e.g., % lift in activation, reduction in churn, X revenue impact).
- Approved roadmap and OKRs for next cycle.
- Repeatable planning and stakeholder communication cadences.

Suggested metrics to track
- Adoption/activation rate, retention/churn, DAU/MAU or relevant engagement metric, conversion rates in critical funnels, feature adoption %, time-to-market, cycle time, NPS/customer satisfaction, revenue or ARR impact.

Ideas for “early wins”
- Reduce onboarding drop-off with a small UX change + microcopy tweak.
- Fix a top customer pain documented in support tickets.
- Remove a friction in checkout/pricing flow that blocks conversion.
- Introduce acceptance criteria and a demo checklist to reduce rework.

Communication & cadence
- Weekly 1:1 with manager with a short agenda (progress, blockers, decisions).
- Biweekly reviews with stakeholders for roadmap updates.
- Monthly metrics/health report to execs.

Short message templates

1) Thank-you to manager / sponsor (quick, professional)
Hi [Manager name], thank you so much for the opportunity and for your support — I’m excited to step into the Senior PM role starting Monday. I’m committed to driving impact quickly and will focus first on learning the product, aligning with stakeholders, and delivering an early win. I’d love to confirm a 30/60/90 success checklist with you — can we schedule 30 minutes this week to align expectations?

2) Short intro to new team (mix of gratitude + engagement)
Hi everyone — I’m [Your name], your new Senior Product Manager. I’m thrilled to join the team and grateful for the warm welcome. My first priority is listening and learning — I’ll be scheduling short 1:1s to understand what’s working, where you need support, and the biggest opportunities. I value clarity, fast learning, and clear outcomes; looking forward to partnering with you. If there’s anything you want me to know before our 1:1, please DM me or drop a note.

Would you like:
- A tailored 30/60/90 plan based on your product type, team size, and top priorities?
- A week-by-week calendar for your first two weeks with suggested meeting timings and agendas?
- A slightly longer intro email for execs or cross-functional partners?

If you tell me product domain, team size, top 2–3 challenges, and whether you inherit an existing roadmap or build a new one, I’ll customize the plan and messages.

messages.speaker: persona_agent
messages.content: I’m over the moon — this promotion means so much to me; it’s a huge boost to my confidence and makes me feel recognized! I’m leading a B2B SaaS analytics product, my team is six (2 PMs, 3 engineers, 1 designer), and our top challenges are low activation, slow release cadence, and fuzzy prioritization — I’m inheriting an existing roadmap but have room to reshuffle.

messages.speaker: responder_agent
messages.content:
Love this — congrats again. Below is a tailored 30/60/90 plan for a B2B SaaS analytics product with a 6-person team (2 PMs, 3 engineers, 1 designer), plus a practical week-by-week schedule for your first two weeks and three short message templates (manager, team, co-PM). I focused on the three challenges you named: low activation, slow release cadence, and fuzzy prioritization.

Quick assumptions I used
- Activation = time-to-first-value (TTFV) / first key action for new accounts.
- You have instrumentation/analytics access (if not, make that a Day 1 priority).
- You’re inheriting a roadmap but can reshuffle priorities.

30/60/90 plan (high-level goals + concrete activities)

30 days — Learn, baseline, and get one quick win
Goals
- Understand product, customers, metrics and the roadmap.
- Baseline activation funnel and release process.
- Build trust with your team and stakeholders.
- Deliver one small, measurable early win for activation or process.

Key activities
- 1:1s: manager (60m), co-PM (60m), each engineer (30m), designer (30m), product marketing, sales/CS leads, support lead (30–45m). Ask: biggest pain, biggest opportunity, what to stop/start/continue.
- Analytics deep-dive: map the activation funnel (events, drop-off points, TTFV definition). Get or add instrumentation where missing.
- Release process review: current cadence, deployment frequency, CI/CD state, blockers, pipeline times.
- Roadmap review: identify 3 items that most affect activation or cadence.
- Customer/contact calls: sit in on 2–3 customer calls or read recent NPS/support threads.
- Quick experiment: pick one low-effort change (microcopy, remove friction in signup, tweak onboarding checklist, short tour) and A/B test.

Deliverables / success signals
- One-page product state with baseline KPI numbers: activation rate, TTFV, release frequency, cycle time.
- A prioritized list of 3 immediate bets (one focused on activation, one on cadence/process, one on prioritization).
- Launched one small experiment and instrumented it.

Suggested metrics to set baseline for
- Activation rate (e.g., % of new trials completing first value within 7 days).
- Time-to-first-value (median).
- Release frequency (releases/week or month), mean cycle time / lead time.
- PR age, % planned vs unplanned work.

30–60 days — Influence roadmap, improve process, and ship small wins
Goals
- Implement a release/process improvement that increases cadence.
- Run 2–3 experiments that move activation metric.
- Put a clear prioritization framework into place.

Key activities
- Prioritization framework: adopt and socialize a scoring model (e.g., RICE or Impact vs Effort + strategic alignment). Run a prioritization workshop with your co-PM, engineer leads, and designer.
- Release cadence changes: introduce smaller batch sizes, feature flags, a release checklist, or a weekly release window. Pilot trunk-based merges or reduce PR size limits if engineering agrees.
- Execute experiments: iterate on onboarding flows, contextual product tours, or in-app triggers to drive TTFV. Use targeted customer segments (by persona & ARR).
- Process: establish team Definition of Done, acceptance criteria, and a demo/ship checklist to reduce rework.

Deliverables / success signals
- New prioritization rubric and updated backlog with top priorities aligned.
- Release/playbook changes implemented (e.g., reduced lead time by X%, started weekly releases).
- Clear experiment results with next steps (iterate/scale/kill).

Targets (example, tune after baselines)
- Increase activation rate by 10–20% on the experiment cohort.
- Reduce mean cycle time or PR age by 20–30%.

60–90 days — Deliver measurable impact and lock in cadence
Goals
- Deliver one medium roadmap item tied to activation or retention.
- Cement release cadence and prioritization as repeatable team practice.
- Present 3–6 month roadmap and OKRs to manager/execs.

Key activities
- Launch & measure: fully roll out the prioritized roadmap item; monitor adoption and TTFV impact.
- Scale experiments that worked; bake successful changes into product.
- Institutionalize process: weekly release cadence, biweekly prioritization reviews, monthly metrics review with stakeholders.
- Team health & hiring: identify skill gaps and make a hiring/training plan if needed.

Deliverables / success signals
- Measured outcome vs baseline (activation % lift, change in TTFV, improved release frequency).
- Approved roadmap + OKRs and a clear resource plan.
- Repeatable cadence and prioritization rituals adopted by the team.

Week-by-week calendar — first two weeks (practical, timeboxed)

Week 1
- Day 1 (Mon)
  - 30m: Kickoff with manager — expectations & success criteria for 30/60/90.
  - 30m: Team intro (all hands) — high-level priorities and schedule 1:1s.
  - 2–3 hours: Read docs, backlog, analytics dashboards.
- Day 2
  - 60m: 1:1 with co-PM — handoffs, current tickets, roadmap context.
  - 30m: 1:1 with designer — design debt, current UX hypotheses.
  - 60–90m: Product analytics deep-dive with data owner/engineer.
- Day 3
  - 30m each: 1:1s with two engineers.
  - 1 hour: Shadow support or CS call.
  - 2 hours: Map activation funnel and note instrumentation gaps.
- Day 4
  - 30m each: 1:1 with remaining engineer and product marketing/sales contact.
  - 1 hour: Roadmap walkthrough with co-PM + key tickets review.
  - 1–2 hours: Draft one-pager baseline and top 3 risks/opportunities.
- Day 5
  - 60m: Stakeholder intro (ops, marketing, sales leadership) — quick align on priorities.
  - 1–2 hours: Prepare and launch a simple activation experiment (design microcopy or onboarding tweak).

Week 2
- Continue 1:1s with any remaining stakeholders / customers.
- Run initial experiment monitoring, check instrumentation.
- Workshop: prioritization session with PM, designer, engineers (60–90m) to adopt rubric and reshuffle top backlog.
- Release process review session with engineers: identify 2–3 specific improvements to pilot (e.g., feature flags + weekly deploy).
- End of Week 2: present 30-day summary to manager — baseline metrics, top 3 priorities, and planned experiments/process changes.

Prioritization rubric (simple & fast)
- RICE (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) OR
- Impact vs Effort matrix + strategic weight:
  - Impact (customer value / revenue), Effort (engineering days), Risk, Strategic alignment.
- Use the rubric to produce a top-6 backlog; everything else is deferred or gated.

Concrete early-win ideas for your context
- Onboarding: measure TTFV; add a short in-app checklist + one contextual tooltip that guides users to the first analytics insight. A/B test with tracked conversion.
- Activation email series: add a behavioral email triggered when users don’t complete the first key action within 48 hours.
- Release/process: pilot weekly small releases using feature flags to decouple deploy from release; measure deployment frequency and rollback rate.
- Prioritization: run a 90-min impact mapping session to remove fuzzy items and align on the next sprint’s scope.

Three short message templates

1) To your manager / sponsor
Hi [Name], thank you again for this opportunity — I’m excited to start as Senior PM on Monday. I’ll focus first on mapping the activation funnel, stabilizing release cadence, and tightening prioritization. Could we meet 30 minutes this week to align on success metrics and any top stakeholder concerns I should be aware of?

2) Short intro to your team
Hi team — I’m thrilled to join as Senior PM. My first priority is listening: I’ll schedule short 1:1s so I can understand current work, blockers, and where you want my support. In week one I’ll be mapping our activation funnel and looking at our release process. I value clarity and fast learning — please DM me anything you want me to know ahead of our 1:1. Looking forward to partnering closely.

3) Note to co-PM (collaborative)
Hey [Co-PM name], excited to work together. Can we book 60 minutes Monday to sync on roadmap ownership, current commitments, and handoffs? I’d like to align on how we’ll split priorities and ensure we present a united plan to the team.

Final notes and next steps
- If you want, I can:
  - Draft the 30-day one-pager template (baselines + top 3 opportunities).
  - Build a prioritized backlog using RICE if you paste your top 10 items.
  - Create the week-by-week calendar as calendar invites with agendas.
  - Recommend specific instrumentation events to track TTFV and activation.

Would you like the one-pager template and a prioritized checklist for the first experiment (exact funnel events, sample microcopy, and A/B test setup)?

messages.speaker: persona_agent
messages.content: I’m still buzzing — I keep replaying the moment my boss called to give me the news! Yes please — could you draft the 30‑day one‑pager (baselines + top 3 opportunities) and the prioritized checklist for the first activation experiment with exact funnel events, sample microcopy, and an A/B test setup, plus a 30‑minute manager meeting agenda?

messages.speaker: responder_agent
messages.content:
Fantastic — congrats again. Below are three ready-to-use deliverables you can drop into Monday’s work: (A) a 30‑day one‑pager (baselines + top 3 opportunities), (B) a prioritized, actionable checklist for the first activation experiment with exact funnel events, sample microcopy, and an A/B test setup, and (C) a timeboxed 30‑minute manager meeting agenda with pre-reads and desired outcomes.

A) 30‑day one‑pager — Baselines + Top 3 opportunities
- Context
  - Role: Senior PM for B2B SaaS analytics. Team: 2 PMs, 3 eng, 1 designer. Inheriting roadmap; focus: increase activation, speed up release cadence, clear prioritization.
- Baseline metrics (fill numeric values after Day 1 analytics review)
  - Activation rate: % of new accounts that complete the defined “first value” within 7 days = ___% (current)
  - Time-to-first-value (TTFV): median time from trial/signup to first insight = ___ hours/days
  - Release frequency: releases per week/month = ___
  - Mean cycle time / lead time: avg days from ticket accepted to release = ___
  - PR age / % planned vs unplanned work = ___
- Top 3 opportunities (priority, why it matters, recommended first action, success metric)
  1) Improve activation by guiding new users to first insight
     - Why: activation is low and TTFV long → lower trial conversion and CVR.
     - First action: launch an in‑app onboarding checklist + contextual tooltip that leads users to the first “aha” (connect data → run query → view dashboard/insight).
     - Success metric: +relative increase in activation rate for experiment cohort (target initial lift: +10–20%).
  2) Speed up release cadence with small-batch deploys & feature flags
     - Why: slow cadence increases risk and delays learning.
     - First action: pilot weekly small releases using feature flags and a release checklist; reduce PR size limits and introduce a demo/ship checklist.
     - Success metric: increase release frequency by X → reduce mean cycle time by 20–30% within 30–60 days.
  3) Remove fuzzy prioritization with a lightweight scoring rubric
     - Why: roadmap reshuffle needed to focus on activation/cadence wins.
     - First action: run a 90‑min prioritization workshop adopting RICE (or Impact×Effort + strategic weight) and produce a top‑6 committed backlog.
     - Success metric: agreed top‑6 backlog; 80% of sprint capacity committed to prioritized work (less ad‑hoc work).
- Deliverables by Day 30
  - One‑page baseline (metrics populated) + top 3 bets
  - Prioritized top‑6 backlog
  - Live A/B experiment for onboarding (see checklist below)
  - Suggested OKR draft for next cycle (Activation TTFV, Release cadence metric, Prioritization adoption)

B) Prioritized checklist for the first activation experiment (in‑app onboarding checklist + contextual tooltip)
Goal: reduce TTFV and increase % of new accounts reaching “first insight” within 7 days.

1) Define the funnel and exact events to instrument (names + definitions)
- Event: Account Created
  - Properties: account_id, plan, org_size, signup_source, timestamp
- Event: Email Verified (if applicable)
  - Properties: account_id, user_id, timestamp
- Event: Data Source Connected (FirstDataSourceConnected)
  - Properties: account_id, user_id, datasource_type, timestamp
- Event: First Dashboard Viewed (FirstDashboardViewed)
  - Properties: account_id, user_id, dashboard_id, timestamp
- Event: First Query / Insight Created (FirstInsightCreated)
  - Properties: account_id, user_id, insight_id, insight_type, timestamp
- Derived metric: TimeToFirstValue = timestamp(FirstInsightCreated) - timestamp(Account Created)
- Activation (primary conversion): user/account that has FirstInsightCreated within 7 days of Account Created

2) Experiment concept & hypothesis
- Hypothesis: adding a short in‑app onboarding checklist + a contextual tooltip that drives users to connect a data source and create their first insight will increase activation rate within 7 days by X% (target 10–20% uplift).
- Variant B (treatment): show checklist + tooltip + follow-up behavioral email if not completed in 48 hours.
- Control: existing onboarding (no checklist/tooltip/email).

3) Prioritized implementation checklist (order, owner, time estimate)
- PM: final scope, success metric, test plan, assign owners (0.5 day)
- Designer: design checklist UI, tooltip placement, microcopy (1–2 days)
- Eng (frontend): implement checklist UI, tooltip, client events (3 days)
- Eng (backend/analytics): add instrumented events, ensure events pipeline and funnel dashboard (1–2 days)
- Product/QA: QA flows across browsers, mobile/responsive, feature flags (1 day)
- PM/Marketing: write follow-up behavioral email and schedule trigger (0.5 day)
- Data Analyst: build funnel dashboard and conversion tracking, cohort analysis template (0.5–1 day)
- Launch & monitor behind a feature flag, ramp to 100% for new trials after QA (0.5 day)
Total initial sprint estimate: ~1–2 sprints depending on capacity (time estimates assume small scope).

4) Sample microcopy (copy to use verbatim or tweak)
- Onboarding checklist header: “Get to your first insight — 3 quick steps”
  - Step 1: “Connect a data source” — CTA: “Connect data” (tooltip: “Connect one source to start seeing live metrics”)
  - Step 2: “Load a sample dashboard” — CTA: “View sample dashboard” (tooltip: “See how your metrics will look”)
  - Step 3: “Save your first insight” — CTA: “Create insight” (tooltip: “Highlight an important metric and share with your team”)
- Contextual tooltip (shown on key screen/button): “Tip: Connect a data source to see live analytics. Click ‘Connect data’ — it takes 2 minutes.”
- CTA button text: “Get my first insight”
- 48‑hour behavioral email (subject + body)
  - Subject: “Need help getting your first insight?”
  - Body: “Hi {first_name}, welcome to {Product}. Many customers see value within minutes by connecting one data source and opening the sample dashboard. Click below to finish setup and get your first insight. [Get my first insight] — Need help? Reply to this email and we’ll walk you through it.”
- Tiny success toast after FirstInsightCreated: “Nice — your first insight is ready. Tip: pin this dashboard to share with your team.”

5) A/B test setup (practical, clear)

- Duration

- Randomization & rollout

- Analysis plan

- Post-test rollout

1) Activation rate and counts for a cohort (accounts created between @start_date and @end_date), activation defined as FirstInsightCreated within 7 days:

-- Cohort activation & TTFV (BigQuery Standard SQL)
WITH account_created AS (
  SELECT account_id,
         MIN(event_time) AS created_at
  FROM `project.dataset.events`
  WHERE event_name = 'Account Created'
    AND event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP(@start_date) AND TIMESTAMP(@end_date)
  GROUP BY account_id
),
first_insight AS (
  SELECT account_id,
         MIN(event_time) AS first_insight_at
  FROM `project.dataset.events`
  WHERE event_name = 'FirstInsightCreated'
  GROUP BY account_id
),
joined AS (
  SELECT ac.account_id,
         ac.created_at,
         fi.first_insight_at,
         TIMESTAMP_DIFF(fi.first_insight_at, ac.created_at, MINUTE) AS ttfv_minutes
  FROM account_created ac
  LEFT JOIN first_insight fi
    ON ac.account_id = fi.account_id
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_accounts,
  COUNTIF(first_insight_at IS NOT NULL AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(first_insight_at, created_at, DAY) <= 7) AS activated_accounts_7d,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(first_insight_at IS NOT NULL AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(first_insight_at, created_at, DAY) <= 7), COUNT(*)) AS activation_rate_7d,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(ttfv_minutes, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS median_ttfv_minutes
FROM joined;

2) Time series: daily activation rate (last 30 days)
-- Daily cohort by account created date
WITH account_created AS (
  SELECT account_id,
         DATE(MIN(event_time)) AS created_date,
         MIN(event_time) AS created_at
  FROM `project.dataset.events`
  WHERE event_name = 'Account Created'
    AND event_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  GROUP BY account_id
),
first_insight AS (
  SELECT account_id,
         MIN(event_time) AS first_insight_at
  FROM `project.dataset.events`
  WHERE event_name = 'FirstInsightCreated'
    AND event_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 37 DAY) -- allow 7-day window
  GROUP BY account_id
)
SELECT
  ac.created_date,
  COUNT(*) AS new_accounts,
  COUNTIF(fi.first_insight_at IS NOT NULL AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(fi.first_insight_at, ac.created_at, DAY) <= 7) AS activated_within_7d,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(fi.first_insight_at IS NOT NULL AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(fi.first_insight_at, ac.created_at, DAY) <= 7), COUNT(*)) AS activation_rate_7d
FROM account_created ac
LEFT JOIN first_insight fi ON ac.account_id = fi.account_id
GROUP BY ac.created_date
ORDER BY ac.created_date;

B) Mixpanel approach
Preferred: use Mixpanel Funnel report (UI) to get activation % quickly:
- Funnel steps: Account Created → FirstInsightCreated
- Conversion window: 7 days
- Segment by signup_source / plan to see differences
This gives activation rate and per‑step conversion quickly.

If you want JQL to compute TTFV per account and cohort, here’s a starter JQL (adapt dates and property names):

/* Mixpanel JQL: per-account created_at and first_insight_at, output ttfv in minutes */
function main() {
  var start = "2026-04-01";
  var end = "2026-04-30";
  var creations = Events({
    from_date: start,
    to_date: end,
    event_selectors: [{event: "Account Created"}]
  }).groupByUser(function(e){ return e.distinct_id; }, mixpanel.reducer.min("time"));

  var firstInsights = Events({
    from_date: start,
    to_date: /* extend to capture 7d window e.g. */ "2026-05-07",
    event_selectors: [{event: "FirstInsightCreated"}]
  }).groupByUser(function(e){ return e.distinct_id; }, mixpanel.reducer.min("time"));

  return creations.join(firstInsights, function(c, f) {
    var created = c.value;
    var first = f ? f.value : null;
    return { distinct_id: c.key[0],
             created_at: created,
             first_insight_at: first,
             ttfv_minutes: first ? (first - created) / 60000 : null };
  });
}

Notes on Mixpanel JQL:
- JQL returns per‑user rows; you can aggregate in the script or export results to compute activation % (count rows with ttfv_minutes <= 7*24*60).
- If your Mixpanel distinct_id is user_id but activation needs account-level aggregation, ensure you have account_id as a super property and aggregate by that instead.

messages.speaker: responder_agent
messages.content:
Love this — huge congrats again. Below is a ready-to-use, practical 30/60/90 blueprint you can adapt and roll out, plus quick wins and communication tips to help you hit the ground running. If you want, I can tailor this to your company (stage, product type, team size) or draft the announcement and first-team meeting slides/notes.

30/60/90 plan (high-level)

First 30 days — Listen, learn, map
- Primary focus: build trust, collect context, and inventory.
- Goals:
  - Meet 1:1 with every direct report and key cross-functional partners (engineering, design, sales, CS, marketing, analytics).
  - Understand current roadmap, backlog, KPIs, and active initiatives.
  - Identify top customer pain points and highest-risk technical debt.
- Key actions:
  - 30–60 minute 1:1s with directs; 30-minute syncs with cross-functional leads.
  - Read product/metrics dashboards, recent retros, NPS/CSAT feedback, and major postmortems.
  - Map team roles, decision rights, and current processes (discovery, prioritization, delivery).
  - Run a quick “state of product” audit: roadmap health, CI/CD cadence, cycle time, release stability.
- Early deliverables:
  - One-page “current-state” summary and list of top 3–5 opportunities/risks.
  - Initial 30/60/90 high-level priorities shared with your manager and leads.
- Metrics to watch: activation/activation funnel, feature adoption, sprint predictability, deployment frequency, defect rate.

30–60 days — Prioritize, prove, and implement early process changes
- Primary focus: secure early wins, start fixing the biggest friction points, and introduce lightweight process improvements.
- Goals:
  - Deliver 1–2 visible, measurable early wins.
  - Establish a standardized discovery-to-delivery flow and decision-making framework.
  - Create clear success metrics (OKRs) and ownership for top initiatives.
- Key actions:
  - Prioritize backlog using impact/effort, customer value, and strategic fit. Run a prioritization workshop.
  - Launch 2–3 experiments/quick fixes that can move KPIs within 30–60 days (e.g., onboarding flow A/B test).
  - Introduce ceremonies or templates: PRD template, experiment template, definition of ready/done, triage board.
  - Set cadence for product reviews and stakeholder syncs (weekly roadmap sync, monthly stakeholder review).
- Early deliverables:
  - A prioritized “90-day wins” roadmap with owners, metrics, and timelines.
  - New or updated templates and a short playbook for discovery and delivery.
- Metrics to watch: experiment lift (e.g., % activation increase), cycle time reduction, stakeholder satisfaction.

60–90 days — Scale, embed culture, and set long-term direction
- Primary focus: embed process improvements, staff/hire where needed, and align product strategy with business goals.
- Goals:
  - Launch/iterate larger initiatives based on validated learnings.
  - Cement ownership and career paths; empower team to own outcomes end-to-end.
  - Align product roadmap to company OKRs for the next quarter/year.
- Key actions:
  - Roll out scaled discovery practices (customer interviews, JTBD mapping, continuous user research).
  - Formalize metrics and dashboards for product health and outcome ownership (weekly/biweekly reviews).
  - Address resourcing needs (hiring plan, contractors, re-org if necessary).
  - Establish product coaching and mentoring cadence (pairing, reviews).
- Early deliverables:
  - Updated roadmap tied to company OKRs and a hiring/re-org proposal if needed.
  - Clear RACI for major product decisions and a published team charter.
- Metrics to watch: OKR progress, retention/engagement, time-to-value for new features.

Concrete early-win ideas (pick 1–2 to start)
- Improve onboarding conversion with a short A/B test (copyflow, progress indicators) — measurable in weeks.
- Triage and remove 20% of low-value backlog items to improve focus and velocity.
- Fix the top 3 support pain points that cause repeated tickets — reduce support load.
- Deploy a small performance or reliability fix that improves user experience and PR messaging.
- Run a rapid customer interview sprint and synthesize into 3 product hypotheses.

How to empower the team to own outcomes
- Set clear outcome-based goals (not feature to-dos). Example: “Increase 30-day retention by X%” rather than “Build feature Y.”
- Assign owners for outcomes with authority to make tradeoffs; document decision rights (RACI).
- Use short, measurable experiments as the primary learning mechanism; reward validated learning.
- Create career ladders and clear success criteria for PMs (impact, leadership, craft).
- Remove blockers actively (tech debt budget, prioritization clarity, stakeholder alignment).

Quick communication plan
- Day 1–3: Short email/announcement introducing yourself, your approach, immediate priorities, and how you’ll engage (offer to draft this).
- Week 1 all-hands: High-level vision, listening tour schedule, and what you expect from team in the next 30 days.
- Ongoing: weekly leadership sync, biweekly product reviews, monthly stakeholder updates.
- 1:1 cadence: weekly with directs for first 90 days; ensure time for coaching and unblockers.

Templates I can create for you (pick any)
- A tailored 30/60/90 slide or doc for your execs.
- Announcement email + first-team meeting agenda and talking points.
- 1:1 template to standardize conversations.
- Prioritization workshop agenda and decision rubric.
- Experiment/PRD template and a RACI matrix.

Next step — how I can help right now
- I can draft your 30/60/90 slide/doc and the Day 1 email.
- Or I can create the first-team meeting talking points and a 1:1 template.

Tell me:
- Company stage (startup / scale-up / enterprise)
- Product type (SaaS, consumer, marketplace, hardware, etc.)
- Team size and direct reports
- Any immediate fires or time constraints

Which deliverable do you want me to draft first?

messages.content: I’m riding a huge confidence boost from this promotion and feel truly valued — please draft a tailored 30/60/90 slide/doc plus a Day 1 announcement email. messages.speaker: responder_agent
messages.content:
Fantastic — congrats again. Below are two ready-to-use assets you can copy/paste and adapt: (A) a concise 30/60/90 slide/doc blueprint tailored for a scale-up SaaS with a ~15-person product org and 4 direct PMs, focusing on backlog/prioritization and onboarding conversion; and (B) a Day 1 announcement email you can send to the product org and key partners.

A. 30/60/90 slide / one-page doc (slide-by-slide content + speaker notes)
Use this as a short slide deck (6–8 slides) or a one-page doc. Replace placeholders (names, baseline numbers) as needed.

Slide 1 — Title
- Title: 30 / 60 / 90 Plan — Product
- Subtitle: Director of Product — [Your Name] | Date
- Speaker note: Quick, upbeat intro: 1–2 lines about joining and commitment to outcomes.

Slide 2 — Objectives (first 90 days)
- Primary goals:
  - Stabilize prioritization & reduce backlog noise
  - Improve onboarding conversion (fast measurable lift)
  - Build trust & clarity across PMs and cross-functional partners
  - Deliver 1–2 visible wins to build momentum
- Speaker note: Frame as listening first, then focused interventions.

Slide 3 — Current-state snapshot (one-liner bullets)
- Product org: 15 people; 4 PM directs
- Biggest friction: chaotic backlog/prioritization; unclear decision rights
- Key metric to move fast: onboarding conversion (current baseline: [insert %])
- Other relevant signals: long cycle-time, repeated support tickets related to onboarding
- Speaker note: Acknowledge strengths and constraints briefly.

Slide 4 — 30 days — Listen, audit, quick fixes (focus)
- Goals:
  - Complete listening tour with all directs & key cross-functional leads
  - Deliver one-page current-state and top 3 opportunities/risks
  - Baseline onboarding funnel & backlog metrics
- Actions (weeks 1–4):
  - 1:1s with 4 directs + engineering, design, analytics, CS, sales (30–60m)
  - Run a rapid backlog triage: identify top 20% low-value items to archive
  - Launch a 2-week onboarding audit (funnel, session recordings, user feedback)

- Deliverables:
  - One-page “current state” + prioritized list of 90-day wins
  - Experiment plan for onboarding improvements
- Metrics to baseline: onboarding conversion %, activation time, backlog size by priority

Slide 5 — 30–60 days — Prioritize & prove (focus)
- Goals:
  - Deliver 1 measurable early win (onboarding experiment)
  - Introduce simple prioritization framework and triage process
  - Define outcome-based goals with owners
- Actions (weeks 5–8):
  - Run 1–2 rapid onboarding experiments (A/B test UX copy, reduce steps, email flow)
  - Host prioritization workshop: adopt RICE or Impact/Effort + OKR alignment
  - Create templates (experiment brief, PRD-lite, definition of ready/done)
  - Publish 90-day wins roadmap with owners & metrics
- Deliverables:
  - Experiment results & decision (iterate/rollout)
  - New prioritization rubric + archived low-value backlog items
- Metrics to watch: % lift in onboarding conversion, experiment lift, backlog trimmed (%), cycle time

Slide 6 — 60–90 days — Scale & embed (focus)
- Goals:
  - Embed discovery-to-delivery workflow and outcome ownership
  - Roll out validated onboarding improvements and start larger initiatives
  - Align roadmap to company OKRs and hiring needs
- Actions (weeks 9–12):
  - Formalize weekly product health dashboard and stakeholder cadence
  - Start hiring or reallocate resources if gaps found
  - Introduce continuous user research cadence (customer interviews / JTBD mapping)
  - Set career/craft checkpoints for PMs
- Deliverables:
  - Roadmap aligned to OKRs, RACI for key decisions, team charter
- Metrics to watch: OKR progress, onboarding conversion sustained lift, retention, sprint predictability

Slide 7 — Early-win ideas & owners (pick 1–2)
- High-impact quick experiments:
  - A/B test onboarding flow (copy + progress indicator) — owner: PM A / analytics
  - Simplify sign-up -> activation path by removing 1 friction step — owner: PM B / Eng
  - Triage & archive 20% low-value backlog items — owner: PM lead / Eng manager
  - Fix top 3 support issues causing repeated onboarding tickets — owner: PM C / CS
- Suggested success criteria (examples):
  - +X% onboarding conversion after 2–4 weeks vs baseline
  - Backlog reduced by 20% with clear rationale and re-prioritized top 10 items

Slide 8 — Cadence, asks & next steps
- Cadence:
  - Weekly 1:1s with directs (first 90 days)
  - Weekly product triage (30m) + weekly dev sync (if needed)
  - Biweekly product review with stakeholders
  - Monthly roadmap/OKR review with execs
- Immediate asks (for leadership/partners):
  - Access to dashboards, analytics, user session recordings, current backlog
  - Time on calendars for 1:1s in next 7–10 days
  - Decision support for trimming backlog and running experiments
- Next step:
  - Day 1 all-hands (intro + listening tour schedule)
  - Run backlog triage in week 1–2 and onboarding audit in week 1
- Speaker note: End with an invitation for feedback and collaboration.

B. Day 1 announcement email (ready to send)
Subject: Quick hello + my priorities and listening tour (Director of Product)

Hi team —

I’m thrilled to join you as Director of Product. Thank you for the warm welcome so far — I’m excited to roll up my sleeves and partner with you to make our product clearer, faster, and more valuable for users.

Quick overview of my approach
- Listen first: I’ll spend the first 30 days learning from you, our partners, and our customers.  
- Focus on outcomes: We’ll prioritize by the impact on customers and business outcomes, not by feature activity.  
- Move fast with experiments: Small, measurable experiments will guide our decisions before heavy investment.

Immediate priorities (first 90 days)
1) Tame the backlog & prioritization — establish a simple, repeatable rubric and archive low-value work so we can focus.
2) Improve onboarding conversion — run rapid experiments to reduce friction and prove early lift.
3) Build clarity & cadence — clear owners, metrics, and a lightweight playbook for discovery → delivery.

What I’ll do in week 1
- Schedule 1:1s with each of you (direct reports + key partners). Please accept the invite or propose a better time.  
- Run a quick onboarding audit and baseline the funnel (analytics + session recordings).  
- Kick off a backlog triage: I’ll ask each PM to bring a short list of items to keep/kill/prioritize.

How you can help
- Share access to the product dashboards, backlog board, and recent customer research.  
- Send me any red flags you want me to see first (top support tickets, live issues, or stakeholder tensions).  
- Be candid — I want to understand what’s working and where we can improve.

First team sync
I’ll hold a short all-hands on Day [X] to introduce myself, share the listening tour schedule, and answer questions. Expect an invite shortly.

I’m genuinely excited to work with each of you. My door is open — feedback, ideas, and constructive pushback are welcome.

Best,  
[Your Name]  
Director of Product

Optional short PS to execs/stakeholders (if sending broader)
PS — I’ll follow up with a one-page current-state and proposed 90-day wins for exec review by end of week 1.

— End —

If you’d like, I can:
- Convert the slide content into a polished Google Slides or PPT file.
- Draft the Day 1 all-hands agenda and talking points.
- Create the backlog triage workshop agenda and a prioritization rubric (RICE template or Impact/Effort + OKR alignment).
- Draft two concrete onboarding experiment briefs (hypotheses, metrics, sample test design).

Which of those next steps do you want me to prepare now?

messages.speaker: responder_agent
messages.content:
Awesome — delighted this fits what you need. I can’t create a Google Slides file directly in your Drive, but I can (A) produce a ready-to-paste slide deck (text + speaker notes) below so you can copy into Slides immediately, and (B) export a PPTX you can upload to Drive if you want — tell me the deck title, logo (optional), and whether to include your name/title on the master slide and I’ll generate the file for download.

Below are three deliverables you asked for:
1) Google Slides-ready slide content (slide text + speaker notes) — 8 slides.
2) Day 1 all-hands agenda with exact talking points / script and suggested Q&A prompts.
3) Two concrete onboarding experiment briefs (hypotheses, metrics, test designs, timeline, owners, success criteria, risks).

1) Slide deck content (copy/paste into Google Slides)
Slide 1 — Title
- Title: 30 / 60 / 90 Plan — Product
- Subtitle: Director of Product — [Your Name] | [Date]
Speaker note: Quick upbeat intro — 1 line on gratitude and commitment to delivering measurable outcomes.

Slide 2 — First 90-day objectives
- Stabilize prioritization & reduce backlog noise
- Improve onboarding conversion (fast, measurable lift)
- Build trust & clarity across PMs and partners
- Deliver 1–2 visible wins to build momentum
Speaker note: Emphasize listen-first approach, then focused experiments and process changes.

Slide 3 — Current state (one-page snapshot)
- Product org: ~15 people; 4 direct PMs
- Biggest friction: chaotic backlog/prioritization; unclear decision rights
- Key metric to move: onboarding conversion (baseline = [insert %])
- Signals: long cycle time, repeated support tickets tied to onboarding
Speaker note: Acknowledge team strengths; position next actions as targeted fixes, not wholesale change.

Slide 4 — 30 days: Listen, audit, quick fixes
- Goals:
  - Complete listening tour with directs & cross-functional leads
  - Deliver one-page current-state + top 3 opportunities/risks
  - Baseline onboarding funnel & backlog metrics
- Actions:
  - 1:1s with 4 direct PMs + Eng, Design, Analytics, CS, Sales
  - Rapid backlog triage: identify 20% low-value items to archive
  - 2-week onboarding audit: funnel, session recordings, top support tickets
  - Set weekly product triage (15–30m)
- Deliverables: one-page current-state, onboarding experiment plan
Speaker note: Emphasize speed of audit and the expectation that PMs come prepared with short backlog lists.

Slide 5 — 30–60 days: Prioritize & prove
- Goals:
  - Deliver 1 measurable early win (onboarding experiment)
  - Introduce a simple prioritization framework and triage process
  - Define outcome-based goals with clear owners
- Actions:
  - Run 1–2 rapid onboarding experiments (A/B tests)
  - Host prioritization workshop (RICE or Impact/Effort + OKR)
  - Publish 90-day wins roadmap with owners & metrics
  - Templates: experiment brief, PRD-lite, def. of ready/done
- Deliverables: experiment results, prioritization rubric, trimmed backlog
Speaker note: Frame experiments as cheap learning; early wins are to build credibility and momentum.

Slide 6 — 60–90 days: Scale & embed
- Goals:
  - Embed discovery→delivery workflow and outcome ownership
  - Roll out validated onboarding improvements
  - Align roadmap to company OKRs; address hiring needs
- Actions:
  - Weekly product health dashboard and stakeholder cadence
  - Introduce continuous research cadence (customer interviews, JTBD)
  - Hiring/reorg proposals if needed; clear RACI for decisions
- Deliverables: OKR-aligned roadmap, team charter, RACI
Speaker note: Stress sustainability and that these steps enable the team to ship faster with higher confidence.

Slide 7 — Early-win ideas & owners (pick 1–2)
- Experiment 1: A/B test onboarding flow (copy + progress indicator) — owner: PM A / Analytics
- Experiment 2: Remove 1 friction step in signup -> activation (or simplify required fields) — owner: PM B / Eng
- Backlog: Triage & archive 20% low-value items — owner: PM lead / Eng manager
- Support fixes: Resolve top 3 onboarding-related tickets — owner: PM C / CS
- Success examples:
  - +X% onboarding conversion within 2–4 weeks
  - 20% backlog reduction with prioritized top 10 items
Speaker note: Recommend choosing 1 primary and 1 backup experiment based on analytics availability.

Slide 8 — Cadence, asks, next steps
- Cadence:
  - Weekly 1:1s with directs (first 90 days)
  - Weekly product triage (30m)
  - Biweekly product review with stakeholders
  - Monthly roadmap/OKR review with execs

  - Access to dashboards, analytics, session recordings, backlog board
  - 1:1 time slots in next 7–10 days

Speaker note: Close by inviting feedback and saying you’ll circulate the one-page current-state by EOW.

2) Day 1 all-hands agenda + talking points (30–35 minutes)
Suggested time: 30 minutes (keep tight; leave 10–12 minutes for Q&A)

Agenda
- 0:00–2:00 — Quick intro (who I am, why I joined)
- 2:00–8:00 — My approach and immediate priorities (30/60/90 summary)
- 8:00–12:00 — What I’ll do in week 1 (listening tour, backlog triage, onboarding audit)
- 12:00–18:00 — Expectations & how I’ll work with you (cadence, 1:1s, decision rights)
- 18:00–28:00 — Q&A (pre-collected + live)
- 28:00–30:00 — Next steps & close (what to expect, asks)

Talking points / script (tight, copy/paste ready)
- Intro (0:00–2:00)
  "Hi everyone — I’m [Your Name]. First, thank you for the warm welcome. I’m really excited to work with you. I came here because I believe in this product and in our ability to move faster for users. Over the next 90 days I’ll be listening, learning, and delivering a couple quick, measurable wins."
- Approach & priorities (2:00–8:00)
  "My approach is simple: listen first, prioritize outcomes not features, and run small experiments to prove direction before large bets. My immediate priorities: (1) tame the backlog and make prioritization repeatable, (2) quickly improve onboarding conversion with experiments, (3) bring clarity on owners, metrics, and a lightweight discovery→delivery playbook."
- Week 1 actions (8:00–12:00)
  "This week I’ll be scheduling 1:1s with each direct and with Eng, Design, CS, Analytics, and Sales. I’ll run a short onboarding audit and ask PMs to prepare a short backlog list (keep/kill/prioritize). Expect 15–30 minute triage meetings weekly going forward."
- How I’ll work (12:00–18:00)
  "I’ll meet weekly with my directs, run a weekly product triage, and host biweekly product reviews with stakeholders. I’ll use a simple prioritization rubric and publish a 90-day wins roadmap. Please be candid — early transparency helps us move faster."
- Q&A (18:00–28:00)
  (Have 3 pre-collected questions ready; then open to live)
  Pre-collected prompts to seed:
   - What will change day-to-day for PMs?
   - How will we decide what to archive from backlog?
   - How will success be measured for onboarding experiments?
- Close & next steps (28:00–30:00)
  "Thanks — I’ll follow up with the listening tour schedule and a one-page current-state by end of week. Please send me any urgent flags or access needs — dashboards, session recordings, backlog links."

3) Two onboarding experiment briefs (run in weeks 2–4)

Experiment A — A/B test onboarding UX: Progress indicator + copy refresh
- Goal: Lift onboarding conversion (new signups → activation) within 2–4 weeks
- Hypothesis: Adding a clear progress indicator and clarifying microcopy at the critical onboarding step will reduce friction and increase activation rate by X% (target: +8–12% relative).
- Primary metric: onboarding conversion % (defined as signups → activation event within 7 days)
- Secondary metrics: time-to-activation, drop-off rate at specific step, NPS or first-week satisfaction (if available)
- Segment: All new signups (holdout/experiment split 50/50) or 60/40 to limit risk if sample small
- Test design:
  - Variant A (control): current flow
  - Variant B (treatment): same flow + progress bar at top + revised copy for 2 fields + contextual helper text/tooltips
  - Duration: minimum 2 weeks or until statistical significance (see sample-size note)
  - Sample size: calculate based on baseline conversion and detectable lift; if baseline low, plan to run 2 weeks with 80% power to detect target lift
- Implementation notes:
  - Front-end changes only (low dev cost)
  - Analytics: event for step view, step completion, activation event, and user bucket tag
- Success criteria:
  - Primary: statistically significant lift in onboarding conversion >= target (e.g., +8%)
  - Secondary: no increase in support tickets for the flow; improved time-to-activation
- Rollout plan:
  - Week 2: finalize copy + UI mock, dev tickets, QA
  - Week 3: run A/B test
  - Week 4: analyze, decide to rollout, iterate, or kill
- Owners: PM A (experiment owner), Eng lead (implementation), Analytics (tracking and analysis), Design (mock & microcopy)
- Risks & mitigations:
  - Risk: sample too small -> mitigation: extend test or widen audience
  - Risk: progress bar causes perception of more steps -> mitigation: keep copy focused on benefits, monitor drop-off

Experiment B — Reduce friction by removing one required field and adding email nurture
- Goal: Increase signup-to-activation conversion by removing a friction point and recovering incomplete signups via nurture; target lift: +10–15% relative.
- Hypothesis: Requiring fewer fields lowers initial abandonment; capturing only essential info and using a short email nurture to collect optional info later will increase activation without harming data quality.
- Primary metric: onboarding conversion % (signups → activation within 7 days)
- Secondary metrics: number of completed profiles (later), email open/click rates, churn of nurtured vs non-nurtured
- Segment: New signups (A/B split)
- Test design:
  - Variant A (control): current signup with full required fields
  - Variant B (treatment): minimal required fields (email + password or email + one key field), optional fields presented later in-app; add automated 24–48h nurture email with value proposition and a CTA to return
  - Duration: 3 weeks (to measure both immediate lift and nurture effect)
  - Sample-size: as above — ensure power to detect target lift
- Implementation notes:
  - Backend: ensure optional data can be collected later and associated with account
  - Email flow: 1–2 test emails, short copy, clear CTA with direct link back to onboarding flow
  - Analytics: capture where users drop off, email open/click, reactivated users
- Success criteria:
  - Primary: statistically significant increase in onboarding conversion >= target
  - Secondary: acceptable completion of optional fields over 30 days; no major drop in data quality for downstream teams
- Rollout plan:
  - Week 2: implement minimal signup + email template + tracking
  - Week 3: go live with A/B test
  - Week 4: measure immediate lift and nurture recovery; decide next steps
- Owners: PM B (experiment owner), Eng (signup change), Marketing/CS or Growth (email nurture), Analytics
- Risks & mitigations:
  - Risk: less user data for segmentation -> mitigation: progressive profiling later in UX; instrument events to capture completion rates
  - Risk: nurture emails flagged as spam -> mitigation: use standard templates, domain warm-up, monitor deliverability

Quick experiment checklist (for both experiments)
- Baseline numbers captured before test
- Clear activation event defined and instrumented
- Analytics tags to capture bucket, step views, completions, and error rates
- Support/CS briefed to expect experiment and capture qualitative feedback
- Minimum test duration and sample-size plan documented
- Rollback plan if metrics worsen

Next steps / what I need from you
- Baseline onboarding conversion % (current) and sample daily signups
- Access or screenshots of the current onboarding funnel and tracking (Mixpanel/GA/Amplitude/Segment)
- Owners: who will be PM A and PM B? engineering bandwidth for weeks 2–4?
- Preference: want me to generate a PPTX of the deck for download? If yes, tell me deck title and whether to include logo and your name on the cover slide.

If you want, I’ll:
- Build the PPTX and return for download
- Draft the quick backlog triage template and the prioritization rubric (RICE or Impact/Effort)
- Draft the actual copy variants for Experiment A and the email copy for Experiment B

Which of those follow-ups should I do next?

messages.speaker: responder_agent
messages.content:
Love the details — thanks. I’ll build the PPTX titled “30/60/90 Plan — Product” with your logo and your name on the cover. Before I generate the file I need your logo (PNG, SVG, or JPG) or a URL to it; otherwise I’ll use a clean text-only cover. I can create the PPTX now once you upload or paste the logo. Quick confirmation of what I’ll include on the cover and master slide: Title “30/60/90 Plan — Product”, Subtitle with your name and Director of Product, and date (I’ll set to today unless you prefer another).

Below are the copy variants for Experiment A (A/B progress indicator + copy refresh) and the nurture email for Experiment B. I also included a short note on sample-size expectations given your baseline (7% conversion, ~400 signups/day) so you can plan test length.

1) Copy variants for Experiment A — Progress indicator + microcopy (treatment)
- Progress indicator (visible at top): “Step 2 of 4 — Get set up” (compact progress bar + percentage)
- Headline (treatment): “Almost there — set up takes < 60 seconds”
  - Control likely: current headline (leave as-is)
- Subhead / value line: “We’ll turn this into your workspace. Skip any step for now — you can update later.”
- Field label / helper copy examples (treatment):
  - Field: “Company name” → helper: “This will be shown on invoices (optional).”
  - Field: “Team size” → helper: “Helps us suggest the right plan — you can change later.”
- CTA buttons:
  - Primary CTA (treatment): “Continue — almost done”
  - Fallback shorter: “Continue”
- Microcopy/tooltips for friction points:
  - Password field tooltip: “Use any password — you can sign in with SSO later.”
  - Email verification note (if applicable): “We’ll send a quick link to finish — no long forms.”
- Error-copy (gentle): “That looks like an invalid entry — try again or skip for now.”
- Tone guidance: short, benefit-first, removes perceived cost/time. Use verbs that emphasize speed and payoff (“Almost done”, “Get started”, “Continue”).

Implementation notes for Experiment A:
- Treatment = progress bar + all microcopy replacements above. Keep UI changes minimal (no extra steps).
- Tracking: tag experiment buckets, track step view, step completion, activation event, and support tickets tied to that flow.
- Split: 50/50 or 60/40 if you want to bias toward the control for risk mitigation.

2) Nurture email(s) for Experiment B — Remove one required field + follow-up nurture
- Strategy: require only essential info at signup (email + password), capture other fields later in-app, and send a short 24–48 hour nurture email to bring users back and finish activation.

  - “Welcome — finish setting up in <1 minute”
  - “You’re almost set — complete your account in one click”
- Preheader: “We saved your progress — finish setup and get started”
- Body (short, single-CTA):
  - Hi [First name],
  - We noticed you started signing up for [Product]. Great choice — your account is waiting. Complete setup in under a minute and start [key value/benefit: e.g., “importing data” / “inviting your team” / “seeing first insights”].
  - [Primary CTA button: “Finish setup” — include deep link that restores their state & goes to next step]
  - If you’d prefer help, reply to this email or book a 15-min walkthrough here: [link].
  - — [Your Name], Director of Product, [Company]
- UTM & tracking: add UTM_source=email_onboard1, UTM_campaign=onboard_recovery

Email 2 — 3–5 days after email 1 (if still incomplete)
- Subject: “Need help finishing setup?”
- Body (social proof + help):
  - Hi [First name],
  - Wanted to check in — customers typically see value in [X minutes / X outcomes] after finishing one quick step. Here’s how you’ll benefit: [short bullet 1–2 bullets].
  - [CTA button: “Complete setup”]
  - If you ran into an issue, reply and we’ll help — or schedule a quick call: [link].
  - — [Customer success or Growth contact], [Company]
- Track open/click and reactivation rates; allow opting out if they’re not interested.

Email implementation notes:
- Send from a friendly sender (e.g., “YourName @ Company” or “YourCompany Support”).
- Keep copy mobile-friendly, single CTA, track opens/clicks and final conversion.
- Include small test of subject line variants (A/B) if bandwidth allows.

3) Quick sample-size guidance (practical)
Given baseline onboarding conversion = 7% and ~400 signups/day:
- Daily activations ≈ 400 * 7% = 28/day.
- To detect a small relative lift (e.g., +8–10% relative = ~+0.56–0.70 percentage points absolute) requires many signups; rough numbers:
  - ~10% relative lift (~0.7ppt) → may require ~20k+ signups total (several weeks to months at 400/day).
  - Larger lifts (15–30% relative) are easier to detect faster:
    - ~15% relative → ~49 days (approx).
    - ~30% relative → often detectable within ~10–14 days.
- Recommendation:
  - Use Experiment B (removing a required field + nurture) to pursue bigger, more detectable lift.
  - For Experiment A, accept that small-lift detection may need longer runs or widen audience (60/40 split, target higher-volume segment), or combine micro-metrics (time-to-activation, step completion) for faster signal.

30/60/90 plan — Senior Product Manager (cross-functional roadmap & mentoring)

High-level approach
- 30 days: Listen, learn, and get aligned.
- 60 days: Define strategy and priorities; begin executing.
- 90 days: Deliver first major outcome, optimize cadence, and scale mentorship.

30 days — Learn & Align
- Goals:
  - Build relationships and trust with PMs, Eng, Design, Data, Sales, CS, Ops, and leadership.
  - Get a clear baseline of product health, roadmap status, and top customer/user issues.
  - Identify 1–2 quick wins.
- Key activities:
  - 1:1s with direct reports, product peers, engineering/tech leads, design lead, data lead, sales/CS leads, and your manager (aim for ~20–25 sessions).
  - Audit roadmap, backlog, OKRs, KPIs, user research, and launch history.
  - Review metrics dashboards (DAU/MAU, conversion funnels, retention/churn, revenue impact, NPS).
  - Attend sprint/planning/release meetings and customer support calls.
  - Run a “product health” assessment (risks, dependencies, tech debt).
- Deliverables (end of 30 days):
  - Stakeholder map and communication plan.
  - Product health brief + list of top 5 risks/opportunities.
  - 1–2 proposed quick-win initiatives with owners and timelines.
- Success metrics:
  - 90% of planned 1:1s completed.
  - Baseline metrics documented and shared.
  - Quick-win(s) scoped and greenlit.

60 days — Strategize & Prioritize
- Goals:
  - Align stakeholders on priorities and draft a clear roadmap.
  - Start structured mentoring for junior PMs.
  - Build consensus on success metrics and resource needs.
- Key activities:
  - Facilitate a cross-functional roadmap workshop to align on goals and trade-offs.
  - Define/update product OKRs and success metrics for top initiatives.
  - Prioritize epics using a clear framework (impact, effort, risk).
  - Establish PM development plan: mentorship cadence, skill goals, shadowing.
  - Kick off discovery/experiments on top-priority initiatives.
- Deliverables (end of 60 days):
  - Draft 6–12 month roadmap with prioritized initiatives and dependencies.
  - Signed-off success metrics and measurement plan.
  - Mentorship plan and schedule for junior PMs.
  - Experiment/validation plans for key hypotheses.
- Success metrics:
  - Roadmap alignment confirmed by key stakeholders.
  - At least one experiment launched and tracked.
  - Mentorship plans in place and first check-ins completed.

90 days — Execute & Scale
- Goals:
  - Deliver the first major milestone and demonstrate measurable impact.
  - Embed effective cross-functional processes and scale PM coaching.
  - Iterate on the roadmap using outcome data.
- Key activities:
  - Coordinate delivery and remove blockers; run sprint demos and retrospective improvements.
  - Measure outcomes vs baseline; present results to leadership and stakeholders.
  - Create onboarding/playbook materials and run PM skill workshops.
  - Optimize release and stakeholder communication cadence.
  - Identify hiring or resource needs and raise them with leadership.
- Deliverables (end of 90 days):
  - Major feature/initiative shipped or significant milestone reached.
  - Outcome report comparing results to baseline (metrics + learnings).
  - Updated roadmap and plan for next quarter.
  - PM playbook/mentorship retrospective summarizing progress.
- Success metrics:
  - Improvement on at least one key product metric (e.g., conversion, retention, NPS).
  - Stakeholder satisfaction (survey or qualitative feedback).
  - Observable growth in junior PMs’ autonomy and skill.

Communication & cadence (recommended)
- Weekly: 1:1s with direct reports and your manager.
- Biweekly: Cross-functional sync (standup/triage) for active initiatives.
- Monthly: Roadmap/metrics review with stakeholders.
- Quarterly: Roadmap refresh and retrospective.

Common risks & mitigations
- Misalignment across stakeholders — mitigation: early workshops and a transparent prioritization framework.
- Scope creep/resource limits — mitigation: enforce guardrails, use OKR trade-offs.
- Slow adoption of new PM processes — mitigation: quick wins, playbooks, and targeted coaching.

Quick-win examples you can pursue immediately
- Fix the top 1–2 user-reported friction points (fast UX fixes).
- Reduce time-to-value in onboarding flow (A/B test copy or funnels).
- Improve release notes/communications to decrease support load.

messages.content:
Awesome — congrats again. Below is a focused, practical 30/60/90 plan with concrete quick wins and a stakeholder meeting map you can use to build credibility fast while protecting your energy.

High-level approach
- Week 1–2: listen, learn, stabilize. Build rapport, remove obvious blockers, set immediate expectations.
- Month 1–2: diagnose and deliver quick wins. Start influencing direction and proving impact.
- Month 3: scale influence, lock a strategy and operating cadence, hand off ongoing work so you don’t own everything.

30/60/90-day plan (Senior Product Lead — strategy + small team)

Days 0–30 (Listen, stabilize, quick wins)
Objectives
- Establish credibility through rapid relationship-building and early, visible wins.
- Learn the product, metrics, roadmap, and top pain points.
Actions
- 1:1s with each direct report (30–60 min) — roles, blockers, career goals, immediate wins they can own.
- 1:1 with your manager (60 min) — expectations, success metrics, key stakeholders, budget/hiring constraints.
- Core cross-functional syncs: eng lead, design lead, data/analytics, CS, sales, QA (30–45 min each).
- Review top metrics/dashboard, current roadmap, backlog, active sprints, highest-severity bugs.
- Deliver 1 clear quick win (examples below).
- Publish a one-page “first 30-day view” summary: what you learned, immediate actions, and how you’ll communicate going forward.
KPIs / success signals
- 100% of 1:1s completed; clear list of top 5 product risks/opportunities.
- Quick win shipped or blocker removed within 30 days.
- Positive feedback from manager or key stakeholders after updates.

Days 31–60 (Diagnose, influence, second wave of wins)
Objectives
- Validate assumptions, prioritize roadmap, put early strategy shape in place.
- Deepen relationships and create repeatable processes.
Actions
- Run a stakeholder alignment workshop (60–90 min) to align on top outcomes and tradeoffs.
- Work with data to set or refine success metrics and dashboards for priority areas.
- Implement or improve one team process that speeds delivery (e.g., triage workflow, definition of done, weekly planning).
- Launch 2nd quick win (bigger than first): e.g., conversion lift, performance improvement, critical UX fix, or automation that saves ops time.
- Set 30–90 day OKRs or success metrics shared with stakeholders.
KPIs / success signals
- Workshop outcomes agreed and documented; ownership assigned.
- New/updated dashboards in place; baseline metrics defined.
- Process change adopted by team and measured (e.g., reduced cycle time, fewer rollbacks).

Days 61–90 (Scale, embed strategy, hand off)
Objectives
- Cement strategic direction and operating model; delegate ongoing ownership for sustainability.
- Demonstrate measurable impact and roadmap for next 6–12 months.
Actions
- Present a 90-day review + proposed 6-month roadmap to manager and key stakeholders.
- Institutionalize cadences: weekly product sync, monthly roadmap review, quarterly planning.
- Identify hiring/training or budget needs; propose plan.
- Delegate operational tasks to direct reports; put in place coaching/mentoring rhythm.
KPIs / success signals
- Clear 6-month roadmap with prioritized bets and expected outcomes.
- Measured improvement on initial KPIs from days 0–30.
- Team demonstrates functioning cadence without you running every meeting.

Suggested quick wins (choose 1–2 in first 30 days)
- Fix the highest-impact UX friction that affects conversion or retention (example: onboarding drop-off screen).
- Triage and close the top 3 recurring bugs causing customer support load.
- Deliver a tiny feature requested by multiple customers that’s low dev effort but high perceived value.
- Create a realtime dashboard showing 3 key metrics for leadership (activation, retention, revenue).
- Automate a manual reporting step that saves a cross-functional team hours/week.

Stakeholder meeting map — who to meet, when, and why

Priority 1 — First week (must-do)
- Direct reports (all): build trust, understand work, uncover blockers. Agenda: role, current priorities, top 3 risks, what support they need.
- Your manager: alignment on priorities, expectations, reporting, budget.
- Engineering lead: delivery health, tech debt, sprint cadence, risk areas.
- Design/UX lead: design backlog, research artifacts, usability issues.
- Data/Analytics: confirm metrics, instrumentation gaps, urgent data needs.
- Customer Success / Support lead: top customer complaints, churn signals, major accounts at risk.

Priority 2 — Week 2–4 (important)
- Sales / Account Execs: customer commitments, product gaps causing lost deals.
- Marketing / Growth: GTM timing, messaging dependencies.
- QA / Ops / SRE: release stability, on-call issues, deployment cadence.
- Finance: implications for roadmap and prioritization if relevant (revenue targets, cost constraints).

Priority 3 — Month 2–3 (align & influence)
- Key customers or partners (select 2–3): confirm real-world pain and validate roadmap bets.
- Legal / Compliance / HR if product or hiring decisions require them.
- Senior leadership stakeholders: product/strategy fit in org goals.

Meeting types & cadence suggestions
- Intro 1:1s (direct reports + key partners): 30–45 min first meeting; weekly 1:1s thereafter (30 min).
- Cross-functional sync: weekly 30–45 min product delivery meeting (status, blockers, decisions).
- Roadmap/strategy review: biweekly or monthly 60–90 min with execs as needed.
- Stakeholder alignment workshop: 60–90 min (early in month 2).
- Office hours: 1-2 hours every other week for open Q&A (reduces ad hoc interruptions).

Meeting agenda templates (short)
- Intro 1:1 (30 min)
  - 5 min: quick personal intro and role context
  - 10 min: current priorities and top blockers
  - 10 min: expectations and how we’ll work together
  - 5 min: next steps and follow-ups
- Stakeholder alignment workshop (60–90 min)
  - 10 min: goals and desired outcomes
  - 20 min: review current metrics/insights
  - 30 min: brainstorm/prioritize top opportunities/tradeoffs
  - 20 min: agree next steps, owners, timelines

Short scripts / framing to build credibility quickly
- Opening line for 1:1s: “Thanks for meeting — my goal for this month is to listen and unblock. I want to start by understanding your top priorities, what’s slowing you down, and where I can add the most value. What should I know right away?”
- For a cross-functional kickoff: “I’m focused on delivering measurable outcomes. I’d like us to align on one or two measurable priorities this quarter and make sure we’ve got clear owners and visible metrics.”
- When you need to say no / set boundaries: “I want us to do fewer things better. Given our goals and capacity, I can’t do X this quarter without impacting Y. Can we reprioritize or find another owner?”

Credibility-building behaviors (do these every week)
- Share short written updates (1 page or email) with status and decisions — consistent communication builds trust.
- Surface data, not opinions — lead with evidence and customer examples.
- Remove a blocker within 48–72 hours whenever possible (or communicate constraints).
- Empower direct reports: public praise, private coaching, and clear accountability.
- Ask good questions that show you’ve done homework, then listen more than you speak early on.

Burnout-prevention & time management tips (so you can scale leadership sustainably)
- Time block your calendar: reserve 2–3 deep-focus blocks per week (90–120 min each) and protect them.
- Batch 1:1s into a few days rather than spread across the week to create long uninterrupted blocks for deep work.
- Delegate early: assign meeting ownership to direct reports and ask them for 1-line agendas in advance.
- Office hours and asynchronous updates: reduce ad-hoc interruptions and meeting overload.
- Set a weekly wrap-up (15–30 min) to capture wins & alignment; keeps stakeholders informed without extra meetings.
- Use a “no more than 2 major initiatives per quarter” rule to avoid dispersing effort.
- Track your energy: schedule recovery time (even short) and raise capacity concerns early with your manager.

Deliverables you can produce in your first 30 days (templates I can draft for you)
- One-page “First 30-day view”
- 30/60/90 roadmap slide
- Stakeholder meeting agenda templates and follow-up email templates
- Quick win scoping doc (describe problem, owner, success metric, timeline)

- Create meeting email templates (intro 1:1, alignment workshop invite, roadmap review)?
- Sketch a prioritized list of potential quick wins tailored to your product (if you give me the top 2–3 product areas)?

4) Prioritized quick wins — onboarding, activation, retention/churn
Approach: prioritize low-to-medium effort, high-perceived impact wins first (30-day target), then medium-effort wins in 60 days, and larger structural work into 90+ days.

A. Onboarding flow
- Quick Win A1 — Fix the top onboarding drop-off screen
  - Problem: 40–60% drop at step X (complex input/slow validation).  
  - Solution: Simplify form, add inline validation, auto-fill common values, remove nonessential fields.  
  - Success metric: decrease dropoff at that step by 20% (lift activation rate).  
  - Effort: Low–Medium (1–2 sprints).  
  - Owner: PM + Eng + Design.  
  - Target: 14–30 days.

- Quick Win A2 — Add contextual “help” or tooltips for first-time users
  - Problem: Users confused about next action; support tickets spike.  
  - Solution: Add 1–2 contextual microcopy/tooltips and a single short onboarding checklist.  
  - Success metric: reduced support tickets for onboarding topic by 30%; improved first-week retention.  
  - Effort: Low (1 sprint).  
  - Target: 30 days.

- Medium Win A3 — Streamline account setup by enabling social sign-on or progressive profiling
  - Problem: High friction in full-profile flow.  
  - Solution: Allow sign-on options and delay noncritical profile questions.  
  - Success metric: faster time-to-first-value, higher activation rate.  
  - Effort: Medium.  
  - Target: 60–90 days.

B. Activation funnel (first-time meaningful action)
- Quick Win B1 — Identify and instrument the single most meaningful activation event (one dashboard)
  - Problem: Activation KPI unclear or poorly instrumented.  
  - Solution: Work with data to define activation event, create a realtime dashboard, surface to team.  
  - Success metric: baseline activation metric established; funnel visualization in analytics.  
  - Effort: Low.  
  - Owner: PM + Data.  
  - Target: 7–14 days (first step).

- Quick Win B2 — Reduce time-to-first-value (TTFV) by creating a guided first task
  - Problem: Users don’t take the key action that correlates with retention.  
  - Solution: Add a short, guided “first task” flow that leads users to the activation event.  
  - Success metric: improved conversion to activation by 15–25%.  
  - Effort: Medium.  
  - Target: 30–60 days.

- Medium Win B3 — A/B test a simplified CTA or path for new users
  - Problem: Default flow underperforms.  
  - Solution: Implement a 2-arm A/B test with simplified CTA or fewer steps.  
  - Success metric: statistically significant uplift on activation.  
  - Effort: Medium.  
  - Target: 60 days.

C. Retention / churn
- Quick Win C1 — Triage and fix top 3 causes of support-driven churn
  - Problem: Recurring issues in support logs cause cancellations.  
  - Solution: Analyze CS tickets, identify top 3 themes, execute fixes or provide proactive guidance.  
  - Success metric: reduced churn attributable to those issues by 30%.  
  - Effort: Low–Medium.  
  - Owner: PM + Eng + CS.  
  - Target: 30–45 days.

- Quick Win C2 — Launch a “win-back” email for at-risk users based on usage signals
  - Problem: Users show early churn signals but no proactive outreach.  
  - Solution: Define at-risk criteria, trigger personalized emails with tips/offers and product suggestions.  
  - Success metric: lift reactivation by X% (benchmarks depend on current numbers).  
  - Effort: Low.  
  - Target: 30 days.

- Medium Win C3 — Build a retention experiment roadmap (cohort analysis + interventions)
  - Problem: Lack of prioritized retention experiments.  
  - Solution: Run cohort analysis, prioritize experiments (notifications, personalized nudges, feature improvements), run iterative tests.  
  - Success metric: improved 30/60/90-day retention cohorts.  
  - Effort: Medium–High.  
  - Target: 60–90 days and ongoing.

Recommended first 30-day picks (to build credibility fast)
- Instrument activation metric + dashboard (B1) — immediate insight and alignment (7–14 days).  
- Fix top onboarding drop-off (A1) — visible lift in onboarding and activation (14–30 days).  
- Triage top support-driven churn causes and implement fixes or comms (C1) — reduces pain for CS and customers (30–45 days).
